title: 3  Reflection on the MSc Project
text:
3.0.1 Project Summary
My MSc project evaluated the feasibility of using locally hosted Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to computationally integrate and analyse both qualitative and quantitative clinical trial data. Using a dataset from the LQD trial for treatment-resistant depression, I designed and applied three mixed-method analytical tasks: Convergence, Explanatory, and Statistical. Because a human expert baseline was unavailable, I developed an automated “LLM-as-a-Judge” evaluation strategy using custom scoring rubrics to assess the model’s output. The project successfully demonstrated that MLLMs exhibit strong logical reasoning and factual consistency when triangulating clinical data, providing a foundational framework for future computational clinical analysis.


3.0.2 Skills Developed
Throughout the research process, I developed advanced technical data analysis and project management skills, specifically by deploying and configuring language models on a High-Performance Cluster (CREATE). I also significantly enhanced my critical thinking and problem-solving abilities by designing multi-stage “chain-of-thought” prompting pipelines and systematically evaluating the complex logical relationships generated by the AI.


3.0.3 Challenges and Solutions







Challenge
How I Overcame It


Out-Of-Memory (OOM) Errors: Limited computing resources on the HPC caused frequent memory crashes during analysis.
I implemented model quantization to load weights in 4-bit precision, utilized memory-efficient scaled dot-product attention, and divided massive qualitative transcripts into smaller, memory-safe batches.


Clinical Misinterpretation: The model incorrectly assumed a lower QIDS-SR score indicated more severe depression symptoms.
I refined the prompt engineering by adding targeted system prompts that explicitly provided the correct clinical context and scale interpretation.


Data Pipeline Failures: The LLM-generated Python code failed to locate specific data columns in the unseen quantitative dataset.
I updated the prompt instructions to include a detailed glossary of variable names, ensuring the model had the necessary context to generate functional code.

title: 6  Action Plan
text:
6.0.1 Primary Objective: Academic Progression

Pursue Doctoral Studies: My principal career objective remains advancing within academia by identifying and securing a suitable PhD opportunity.
Enhance Funding Competitiveness: Following consultations with academic staff, I have identified that acquiring post-MSc Research Assistant (RA) experience is critical for becoming a highly competitive candidate for PhD funding.
Secure Departmental Research Roles: To bridge this experience gap, I am actively seeking collaborative academic research positions within the department to work alongside established academics in my field.



6.0.2 Secondary Objective: Professional Industry Experience

Develop Applied Data Science Skills: As a strategic alternative, I am concurrently exploring professional employment opportunities within the healthcare sector.
Bridge Academia and Industry: Securing a role in industry will allow me to hone my healthcare data science skills in a practical, real-world setting, which directly supports my ultimate long-term career ambitions following the completion of a PhD.

title: 7  Career Readiness
text:
7.0.1 Technical Profile & Market Positioning

Comprehensive Skill Foundation: Throughout my MSc, I have built a robust and diverse technical repertoire encompassing statistics, data science, machine learning, natural language processing, and advanced Large Language Model (LLM) applications.
Strategic Market Entry: While my academic breadth is extensive, I recognize that I am currently a generalist rather than an industry specialist. To bridge this gap and develop highly specific, industry-ready expertise, I am strategically targeting entry-level to lower-mid-level professional roles.



7.0.2 Academic Pursuits & Professional Development

Doctoral Application Experience: I proactively submitted PhD applications throughout the academic year and successfully passed the rigorous departmental PhD interview. Although I was not nominated for funding this cycle due to limited availability and high competition, the process provided invaluable experience.
Career Strategy & Networking: To continuously refine my trajectory, I have engaged extensively with university career services to optimize my future PhD applications and enhance my networking strategies for the industry job hunt.

title: 10  Summary
text: Reflecting on my MSc journey, bringing together my coursework, technical skill development, and the execution of my dissertation on clinical data integration, I can clearly see my transformation from a student into a capable researcher[cite: 24]. *In hindsight*, the most crucial advice I would give myself at the start of the programme would be to embrace the steep technical learning curve early on and to initiate conversations regarding PhD and career pathways from day one[cite: 24]. Regarding *missing skills*, I quickly realized that while I grasped the theoretical aspects of health data, I initially lacked the advanced computational proficiencies—such as managing High-Performance Clusters (HPC), optimizing Python environments, and utilizing robust version control like Git—that are essential for executing complex, large-scale AI research[cite: 24]. Looking toward *future growth*, my immediate next steps involve securing post-MSc Research Assistant experience to become a more competitive candidate for PhD funding, while simultaneously continuing to hone my applied healthcare data science skills to ensure I am highly prepared for both academic research and professional industry roles.
